title: The self-diagnosis pass runs on every 15 s cycle and costs 18 write transactions and ~83 KB of WAL when nothing has changed
what: notices.run_checks runs at the end of every collector cycle (driven by the 15 s connections kind), commits once per check (17), re-asserts every open notice with an UPDATE plus an unused SELECT id, and rewrites the whole notice_last_checked JSON meta row ~28 times per pass with fresh timestamps nobody reads.
cost: ~7,900 cycles/day (sim_loop.py, default intervals). Per connections-only cycle measured: 18 commits, 29 upserts, 8 UPDATE, 80 SELECT, 83 KB WAL (vs ~8 KB the cycle needs). Per day ~140,000 write-lock acquisitions and ~650 MB WAL on the snapshotted ZFS /data dataset, each commit a lock api_report can queue behind. Same at 4 or 20 machines.
evidence: probe_notices.py: 17 commits / 28 INSERT / 95 KB WAL per pass; probe_cycle.py: 18 commits / 83,020 WAL bytes per cycle with a 15 s clock (12 KB with a frozen clock). ui.py:1912 is the only reader of notice_last_checked and uses only its key set.
fix: Run run_checks only when a kind other than connections ran, or at most every 60 s; keep check-evidence stamps in memory and write the meta row only when the set changes or every ~15 min; in db.notice skip the UPDATE when severity/body/fix are unchanged and last_seen is under ~10 min old. Keep one commit per check and leave a raising check's notices alone.

title: [ OK ] on WHAT THE SERVER CHECKS needs only that a kind was evaluated once, ever: a check that now raises every cycle, or a blind pass, still reads OK
what: The evidence map {kind: last_checked} persists across restarts and the panel only tests key presence, so once stamped a kind is [ OK ] for the life of the database; the timestamps are never read.
cost: A notice check that starts raising (import error after an update, bad row) is only logged and keeps showing [ OK ]; nothing tells anyone (alerts have check_failed, notices do not). The documented stale-stamp behaviour for file_move_detected on a blind inventory pass is not rendered anywhere, so a permanently blind inventory still shows hand-move detection [ OK ], the check whose silence turns moves into deletions (CR-267a).
evidence: Read the only consumer (ui.py:1912) and grepped every reference to NOTICE_CHECKS_META / notice_last_checked.
ledger: new (regression of the intent of resilience sweep 2026-08-28 fix pass finding 1 and dash-collector-alerts-1)
fix: Treat a stamp older than a per-kind bound (3x the writer's cadence, floor 1 h; 2x interval_inventory for file_move_detected) as NOT CHECKED with its age shown, and file a notice when a notice check raises, subject = the check name.

title: remoteneed deletes and re-inserts every unchanged missing-files list every minute
what: For every (folder, device) pair below 100 %, every 60 s, the pass fetches up to 3 pages of /rest/db/remoteneed then DELETEs and re-inserts up to 500 rows with a new refreshed_at whether or not the list changed. No wall-clock budget, unlike completion.
cost: Measured 0.12 MB WAL and 2 ms per pair per pass; 10 incomplete pairs = 1.09 MB/min = ~1.6 GB/day WAL while backlogs last, plus 1-3 remoteneed calls per pair per minute, each an index walk inside Syncthing (estimated tens of ms on a 20k-file folder). Scales with machines x projects behind.
evidence: probe_remoteneed.py: 1 pair 2 ms / 0.12 MB; 10 pairs 17 ms / 1.09 MB per 60 s pass. refreshed_at is read only by fetch_missing and the day-scale prune.
fix: Skip the fetch and rewrite for a pair whose need_items equals the value at its last fetch (force every ~15 min); when fetched, write only if (name, size) differs and otherwise bump refreshed_at with one UPDATE. Keep clear_missing_files for pairs that leave _incomplete and the poll-then-write order.

title: The inventory skip-signature is directory mtimes only, so a file caught mid-copy keeps its partial size and mtime until something else in that project changes
what: Directory mtime changes on create/remove/rename, not when a file grows in place. A walk during a copy written straight to its final name (Explorer/Finder/SMB card copy onto P:) records the partial size and mtime; afterwards the signature matches and the walk is skipped until another entry in that project changes, possibly never.
cost: nas_media size/mtime_ns is the hand-move identity key and the (basename, size) the companion's lane-B found-elsewhere test uses; a later hand move of that clip pairs nothing and is treated as a deletion on every machine (CR-267a re-upload + parked breaker). Project byte totals are short. Per-ingest probability is the overlap of a ~3-hourly walk with a 10-30 min copy: small per copy, recurring on shoot days.
evidence: Read _dir_signature (os.walk + os.stat(dirpath) per directory, no files) and the skip; POSIX/ZFS directory mtime semantics. Not reproduced on the NAS (read-only rule).
fix: After a walk, if any recorded file's mtime_ns is within ~30 min of walked_at, store an unsettled (NULL) signature so the next visit walks the files again. Keep the steady-state no-write skip and CR-297A's forced re-walk.

title: The 8-projects-per-cycle inventory window is spent on unchanged projects too, so 'is it on the server' lags 3 h today and ~16 h at 500 projects
what: The rotating cursor selects 8 projects per 900 s pass and only then compares each one's cheap signature, so an unchanged project consumes a slot; the cap meant to bound the expensive file walk also bounds the cheap check.
cost: Each project is visited every ceil(n/8) passes: 100 projects -> 3.1 h worst case (1.6 h average) before uploaded footage appears in nas_media (MEDIA PRESENCE, locate, hand-move pairing, proxy_pairs); 500 projects -> 15.6 h. replace_nas_media has no other caller.
evidence: Read _run_inventory and the defaults; grep shows the collector is the only refresher of nas_media.
fix: Signature-check all active projects (or a time-budgeted larger window) every pass and spend the 8-walk cap only on changed ones, oldest change first; optionally nudge inventory for a project named in a lane-A upload report. Keep walks before writes, the unmounted canary and the move limits.

title: Invariant 10 (proxy_pairs) re-reads every nas_media row of every project every 15 minutes even when no inventory changed
what: Every invariants pass loads all nas_media rows per active project and rebuilds the original/proxy sets, though the verdict can only change for projects whose inventory was replaced since the last pass.
cost: Measured 2.4 s for 200k rows and 1.58 s for 1M rows (desktop CPU; NAS slower) on the collector thread every 15 min; ~0.3-1 s today, ~8 s+ per pass at 500 projects x 10k files, during which connections/enforce wait.
evidence: probe_proxy_pairs.py: '100 projects x 10000 files = 1000000 rows: 1.58 s'.
fix: Cache each project's verdict in memory keyed on nas_inventory_state.walked_at (or tree_sig) and recompute only changed projects. Keep one subject per Proxy folder and the full found list CR-266c relies on.

title: Syncthing's pending-devices list is fetched on every cycle (~7,900 GETs a day) for a check whose threshold is 24 hours
what: run_cycle calls client.pending_devices() before every self-diagnosis pass, i.e. every 15 s, and its only consumer ignores devices pending less than 24 h.
cost: ~7,900 REST calls/day to the NAS Syncthing; while Syncthing is down each 15 s cycle also waits out the 10 s client timeout on this call.
evidence: probe_cycle.py: pending_devices 1.0 call per connections-only cycle.
fix: Fetch it only when the config kind ran this cycle or at most every 10 min and cache the answer, keeping 'could not ask -> None -> nothing cleared'. Folds into dash-collector-1 if run_checks moves to a slower cadence.
